body:
There is no way to write a multi-ticket DAG into the store atomically. `adlc ticket create --input` takes ONE ticket (packages/tickets/bin → service.planCreate), and looping it cannot build a multi-level DAG: edges live on the BLOCKING ticket and name their dependent, and packages/tickets/lib/schema.mjs:49 rejects `edge to unknown ticket`. So a loop must run in strict reverse-topological order, is non-atomic (a failure at k leaves k-1 tickets active), and emits N unrelated-looking audit entries for one logical operation.

WHAT TO BUILD

`TicketService.planCreateBatch(inputs)` in packages/tickets/lib/service.mjs ONLY. Mirror planCreate (service.mjs:104) exactly, extended to a set:
  - mint an id per ticket via generateTicketId() when absent;
  - reject a duplicate id WITHIN the batch before touching the store;
  - per ticket, call the same guards planCreate calls before mutating: #assertIdNotArchived (ARCHIVE_COLLISION) and #assertNoManifestRails (RAIL_COVERS_MANIFEST, #235). Skipping either opens an unguarded write door past #235;
  - reject an id that already exists in the store (TICKET_EXISTS), same as planCreate;
  - reject a non-array or empty input;
  - push the whole batch in ONE `this.#plan('batch-create', ...)` call so #plan's validateTickets() sees the complete set — that is what makes intra-batch forward edges resolve, and it is the entire reason a loop cannot do this;
  - fileOperations: one {action:'create', id} per ticket; changedFields: the sorted union of keys across the batch.

EVIDENCE BINDING — decided, do not revisit: the plan sets `ticketId: null`, so recordTicketEvidence derives `bindingScope: 'store'` (evidence.mjs:238). The transaction records its normal entry with `operation: 'batch-create'` plus store hashes. Per-ticket provenance is the CALLER's job (its own gate-manifest entries), not the transaction's.

Do NOT emit a `ticketIds` array from the transaction. `ticketIds` is in AUDIT_FIELDS (evidence.mjs:83) and auditFieldsMatch compares every audit field by canonicalJson, so an id array derived at write time must reproduce BYTE-IDENTICALLY on a recovery replay or a resumable recovery becomes a permanent EVIDENCE_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Naming the ids safely requires the journal-v2 work that was explicitly declined.

RAILS: packages/tickets/lib/transaction.mjs and packages/tickets/lib/evidence.mjs are declared rails. The whole point of this shape is that neither changes. If the implementation seems to need either, STOP and say so rather than editing them.

WRITE THE RED TESTS FIRST in packages/tickets/test/service.test.mjs (helpers: `ticket`, `writeDirectory` from ./helpers.mjs):
  - a 3-ticket batch spanning 2 edge levels applies in ONE apply(); all three present; plan.operation === 'batch-create'
  - the same 3 tickets via looping planCreate in forward order FAILS on the unknown edge target — the motivating defect, pinned
  - a batch containing an id already in the store → TICKET_EXISTS, store byte-identical afterwards
  - a duplicate id within the batch → rejected before any write
  - an archived id → ARCHIVE_COLLISION
  - a rail covering the manifest → RAIL_COVERS_MANIFEST
  - a non-array and an empty array → rejected
  - a failed apply leaves the store snapshot hash unchanged
  - the recorded evidence for a batch is store-scoped, i.e. carries no per-ticket binding

ACCEPTANCE
- Every red test above fails before the change and passes after; demonstrate by reverting planCreateBatch and showing them go red.
- `npm test` green from the repo root, output shown.
- `adlc rails-guard --base origin/main --ticket <this ticket id>` exits 0, proving transaction.mjs and evidence.mjs were not touched.
- `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs` exits 0 on the diff.
title: tickets: add planCreateBatch, an atomic multi-ticket write path (#1003)
